reasoning: Herbs and shrubs growing in the understory of forests receive light that has already passed through the canopy of taller trees. The canopy leaves absorb most of the red and blue light for photosynthesis, leaving the light that reaches the forest floor enriched in green wavelengths. Since chlorophyll absorbs green light poorly, the rate of photosynthesis in these plants is significantly lower compared to sun plants that receive full-spectrum white light.
